admission_apply.text: You turn the reed. The silk slips one thread. A high, absent tone brushes the air and fails.

native.admission_inspect: A lacquered reed, bound in pale silk. The silk is warmer than the grain, by a degree you cannot place.
apply_texts: Again the silk shifts, the same width. The missing close of the phrase stays missing.
Nearer still, then not. The silk reverses its fold, as if declining to finish the phrase.
Pale silk resettles. The crack offers the same unfinished cadence, elegant and not quite yours.
The fold reverses. The cadence withdraws what it nearly gave, precise as a courtesy.
The last taut thread loosens without sound. What remains is a polite, unfinished quiet.
The recurrence is smaller, and nearer. You set the reed down before the cadence agrees.
The silk gives. For a moment the crack answers in a pitch too clean to have come from wood.
You almost hear the third pause land. It does not. The reed is only lacquer and thread.
You turn the reed. The silk slips one thread. A high, absent tone brushes the air and fails.
Your fingers find the crack already warm. The almost-note finishes itself, then pretends it did not.
inspect_texts: A lacquered reed, bound in pale silk. The silk is warmer than the grain, by a degree you cannot place.
A pattern almost coheres in the loosened silk: three pauses, then a gap where a cadence should close.
One thread remains taut. The rest hang pale and precise, holding a quiet that will not close.
The reed's crack does not follow the grain. Pale silk covers it, and the silk seems to listen.
The same crack, the same silk. Only the warmth has moved, as if the reed learned a hesitation.
The silk has shifted a thread's width. No name fits the half-tone that almost arrived.
The silk is too smooth. Under it the crack holds a silence shaped like a note you did not sound.
The warmth has withdrawn. The crack waits in the fold it refused, elegant and unfinished.
native.name: Pale Silk Reed
